MIRRLY UPLINK ARCHITECTURE: • Upstream Tunnel defines the physical and cryptographic network route from local SOCKS5 proxy (127.0.0.1:10808) to Telegram data centers via censorship gateways. • Messenger traffic is encapsulated into modern protocols disguised as regular web surfing or tunneled through Cloudflare Anycast infrastructure. • Unlike system VPN, Mirrly operates as a local transparent TCP relay without creating a TUN interface, preventing DNS leaks, battery drain, and OS restrictions.
1. CLOUDFLARE WORKER (WEBSOCKET OVER TLS 1.3): • How it works: traffic traverses an encrypted WebSocket tunnel (port 443) to a serverless V8 function on Cloudflare Edge. Worker connects to Telegram data centers using internal socket API (cloudflare:sockets). • Bypass mechanism: telecom carriers and DPI see a standard HTTPS request with a trusted TLS 1.3 certificate of a global CDN, bypassing protocol inspection. • Quota: Cloudflare free plan offers 100,000 requests per day. Thanks to multiplexing, this quota is virtually impossible to exhaust during everyday use.
2. CLOUDFLARE WARP (MASQUE / RFC 9484): • How it works: state-of-the-art IETF CONNECT-IP / CONNECT-UDP standard over HTTP/3 and QUIC. Connects to Cloudflare Anycast gateways (188.114.96.1) using WireGuard credentials and mTLS certificates (ECDSA P-256). • Advantages: zero Head-of-Line Blocking, minimal round-trip latency, and superior voice and video call quality. • DPI resilience: auto-scans open Anycast ports (500, 8095, 8443, 1074, 443) and applies Noise Handshake Fragmentation.
3. VLESS OVER WEBSOCKET (ANYCAST PAGES CDN): • How it works: lightweight binary VLESS v0 protocol over WebSocket (port 443) with TLS 1.3, masquerading as regular Google Chrome traffic. • Zero-registration: requires no Cloudflare account, API tokens, or custom workers. • Auto pool: includes stable Anycast nodes across Europe and Asia with Happy Eyeballs racing.
4. HYBRID MODE (WORKER + WARP CASCADE): • How it works: two-hop tunneling. Device connects to trusted Worker over WSS, and Worker proxies data to WARP Anycast.

HOW MASQUE WORKS (RFC 9484): • MASQUE (Multiplexing Application Substrate over QUIC Encryption, RFC 9484 / RFC 9298) multiplexes IP packets and UDP datagrams over HTTP/3 and QUIC transport layer. • Traffic routes through the nearest low-latency Cloudflare Edge Anycast server.
AUTOMATIC PROVISIONING & CRYPTOGRAPHY: • Creates WireGuard / Curve25519 keypair and issues a client mTLS certificate (ECDSA P-256) for mutual authentication. • Allocates dedicated internal IPv4 (172.16.0.2) and IPv6 (/128) addresses.
DPI CIRCUMVENTION & HANDSHAKE PACKET FRAGMENTATION: • Bypasses WireGuard handshake filtering via handshake packet fragmentation (splitting init frames below MTU with delayed tail dispatch). • Endpoint scanner automatically finds responsive Anycast ports (8095, 8443, 500, 1074, 443).
AMNEZIAWG EXPORT: • Profile parameters and junk packet headers (Init Packet Magic Header I1) can be copied to clipboard for external AmneziaWG clients.

VLESS PROTOCOL FEATURES: • VLESS is a zero-overhead transport protocol (v0) relying on outer TLS 1.3 encryption without inner cipher duplicates. • Masquerades as standard Google Chrome browser traffic (Chrome utls-mimic) on port 443.
CLOUDFLARE PAGES INFRASTRUCTURE: • Unlike Workers, Pages nodes operate on global Anycast CDN. *.pages.dev domains carry high trust scores in network firewalls and bypass DPI inspections.
DYNAMIC POOL & HAPPY EYEBALLS DUAL-STACK RACE: • Parallel connectivity probing in Rust core (RFC 8305) ensures instantaneous failover between nodes without interrupting active Telegram sessions. • Subscription streaming engine automatically synchronizes verified nodes from GitHub mirrors with strict filtering (pure WSS-over-TLS only; Reality, gRPC, and raw TCP are stripped). • All verified nodes are cached in persistent local device storage.

PORT CONFIGURATION: • Local listening port is the socket on 127.0.0.1 where Telegram client connects. • Port 1080: Standard MTProto port with Fake-TLS. • Port 10808: Standard SOCKS5 transparent TCP relay port.
RECOMMENDATIONS: • Recommended ports: 1080 (MTProto) and 10808 (SOCKS5). They require no root privileges and are standardized for proxy servers. • Allowed range: 1024 to 65535. • If the selected port is occupied by another application, a Bind Error occurs. • Update Telegram proxy link after changing ports via \"Connect Telegram\".

KEY STRUCTURE & CRYPTOGRAPHY: • 32-character hexadecimal (Hex) key used by Telegram to authenticate and encrypt MTProto session headers. • Prefix \'dd\' activates Fake-TLS mode. • With Fake-TLS, initial handshake mimics a standard TLS 1.3 ClientHello with a legitimate SNI domain.
GENERATION & APPLICATION: • Tap the generate icon to create a cryptographically secure random key. • Remember to update your Telegram proxy settings after generating a new key.

CLOUDFLARE WORKER ARCHITECTURE: • Serverless relay routing TCP traffic to Telegram data centers via cloudflare:sockets API. • Entire stream is encrypted end-to-end. ISP sees only HTTPS/WSS requests to a trusted global CDN domain on port 443.
CUSTOM WORKER DEPLOYMENT: • Deploying a personal free worker guarantees dedicated bandwidth, zero shared pool congestion, and complete privacy. • Cloudflare free tier grants 100,000 requests per day per account. • Configured custom domain receives highest priority in Mirrly routing.

HOW IT WORKS: • Listens for the Android BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast event. • Automatically starts the local proxy socket on system startup without requiring manual app launch.
DEVICE-SPECIFIC OEM SETTINGS: • Xiaomi (MIUI/HyperOS): Settings -> Apps -> Permissions -> Autostart -> enable Mirrly TG Proxy. • Samsung (One UI): Add application to \'Never sleeping apps\'. • Huawei (EMUI/HarmonyOS): Switch app launch to manual and toggle \'Auto-launch\'.

WEBSOCKET PRE-WARMING TECHNOLOGY: • Maintains pre-opened standby socket pools (Pre-Warming Pool) and ring buffers in native core to eliminate handshake latency when opening chats or downloading media.
AVAILABLE PROFILES: • Eco (2 sockets, 128 KB buffer): Minimal CPU and RAM footprint (~150 KB). • Balanced (4 sockets, 256 KB buffer): Optimal for everyday messaging. • Turbo (8 sockets, 1 MB buffer): Accelerated media and sticker downloads. • Ultra (16 sockets, 2 MB buffer): Peak throughput for 4K video streams. • Auto (2–16 sockets): Dynamic pool scaling based on bandwidth demands.

NAGLE ALGORITHM (RFC 896): • Controls packet coalescing on local TCP sockets. • Auto: Enables TCP_NODELAY on low latency links (<140ms RTT). • Enabled: Immediate packet dispatch for instant messaging response. • Disabled: Buffers packets, recommended for high packet-loss 2G connections.
POWER SAVING OPTIMIZATIONS: • Disables particle canvas overlays and animations. • Minimizes Compose redraw phases, saving battery on 90-120Hz AMOLED displays.

PROTOCOL COMPARISON: • MTProto (port 1080): Telegram native protocol with Fake-TLS and Flowseal Anycast. • SOCKS5 (port 10808): Transparent TCP Relay (RFC 1928), end-to-end encryption, seamless voice/video calls, supports all upstreams (Worker, WARP, VLESS).

LOCAL SOCKET SECURITY: • By default, 127.0.0.1:10808 socket is open to all local processes. • Setting username and password activates RFC 1929 authentication, preventing unauthorized local apps from using the proxy. • Credentials are automatically embedded into tg://socks links when copied or launched into Telegram.

BATTERY PROTECTION SYSTEM: • Shuts down proxy below configurable battery threshold (5-25%) with a 5-minute notification warning. • One-tap cancellation in notification. • Triggers upon Android system power saver activation. • Thermal QoS scales down pools if battery temperature exceeds 42°C.

ADAPTIVE QOS & THROTTLING: • Dynamically adjusts socket pool size and buffer limits under thermal stress. • Disabled mode runs proxy at peak throughput (16 sockets, 2 MB). • Critical thermal safeguards remain enforced at core level.

DOZE MODE EXEMPTION: • Android freezes network sockets during deep sleep (Doze Mode). • Battery optimization exemption allows proxy to maintain keepalive sockets for incoming Telegram calls and messages. • Minimal idle standby power consumption (~0.1% per day).

DOH CONCURRENT RACING: • Dispatches DNS queries in parallel over HTTP/2 with TLS 1.3. • Fastest valid response wins; lingering queries are canceled. • Validates IP ranges against Telegram AS44907, filtering out poisoned ISP responses.

Creator & Lead Developer of Mirrly TG Proxy
Hello! I am R1Xern — developer of the Mirrly ecosystem.

Mirrly TG Proxy was created to completely solve issues with blocking, throttling, and disruptions in Telegram on Android. The application uses a native C/Rust core, pre-warmed WsPool socket pool, and traffic masking disguised as secure Cloudflare CDN WebSocket connections.
The project runs exclusively locally on your device, ensuring maximum connection stability, optimized speed, and 100% privacy without third-party VPNs.

HOW BILLING WORKS:
• On the Cloudflare Workers Free tier, each account is allocated a quota of 100,000 requests per day.
• Quota reset occurs daily at 00:00 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

WHY WSS SAVES REQUESTS:
• 1 WebSocket connection = exactly 1 Cloudflare request during tunnel establishment (HTTP Upgrade: websocket).
• After tunnel opening, all Telegram data exchange (messages, photos, multi-gigabyte videos, voice calls) flows inside the open socket and DOES NOT generate new requests.

USAGE BENCHMARKS:
• 1 active user uses only 200–800 requests per day (less than 1% of the 100,000 quota).
• Even a group of 10–20 users on a single personal worker consumes no more than 10–15% of the daily limit.

HOW THE COUNTER WORKS:
• The Mirrly TG Proxy analytics module counts requests strictly LOCALLY on your device.
• WSS session opening events by the proxy core and local availability check results are recorded.

ZERO NETWORK OVERHEAD:
• The counter itself makes no external requests to Cloudflare APIs or third-party servers.
• Statistics are stored in the device's encrypted local cache and consume no network traffic.

PURPOSE:
• Number of established secure WebSocket sessions between the proxy and Cloudflare worker.

OPERATING FEATURES:
• Each WSS session encapsulates Telegram data center traffic (DC1–DC5) in a secure TLS 1.3 stream.
• During continuous communication, the socket remains open for hours, consuming only 1 initial request.

PURPOSE:
• Worker health check requests and automatic failover during outages (Multi-Worker Circuit Breaker).

WHEN SENT:
• During manual reachability checks via the "Test" button in Worker Manager.
• During automatic verification of node recovery after network disruption.

HOW IT IS CALCULATED:
• Average number of generated requests per hour over the selected time interval.

FORECASTING:

CLOUDFLARE RULES:

HOW ROUTING WORKS:
• Telegram splits traffic across 5 core data center clusters (DC1–DC5) and the distributed FlowSeal CDN cache network.
• DC 2 (Amsterdam): chats, message synchronization, authorization, and contacts.
• DC 4 (Amsterdam): private media files, voice and video messages.
• FlowSeal CDN: 20 geo-distributed cache servers for high-speed delivery of heavy public channel content.
PURPOSE OF CACHE NODES:\n• Public video files and media from large channels are cached on 20 Telegram CDN nodes.\n• This reduces video download latency and offloads the central DC 4 data center.

ADAPTIVE RESOURCE CONCENTRATION:\n• The engine dynamically allocates WSS pool sockets to the data center with the heaviest current data exchange.\n• During activity pauses, sockets transition into power-saving mode according to exponential decay.

TELEGRAM TRANSPORT TYPES:
• Intermediate (0xee): primary high-speed transport for message exchange.
• Padded Intermediate (0xdd): randomized transport with floating padding to defeat DPI blocking.
• Abridged (0xef): ultra-compact transport for background synchronization.

HOW QUOTA IS SAVED:\n• The ratio indicates how many hundreds of MTProto packets and messages were transmitted inside a single open WSS session.\n• Allows sustaining heavy communication without wasting daily Cloudflare requests.

1. SHANNON POOL ENTROPY (H):
• Formula: H = -∑ p_i * ln(p_i), where p_i is the load share of the i-th data center.
• H < 0.60: High concentration (Single-DC Affinity). Entire capacity focused on one DC (e.g., text chat reading on DC2). Maximum battery and socket savings.
• 0.60 ≤ H ≤ 1.30: Balanced mode (Dual Affinity). Parallel exchange with DC2 (messages) and DC4 (media) or FlowSeal CDN.
• H > 1.30: High-dispersion mode (Multi-Cluster Burst). Simultaneous synchronization, calls, and downloads across all Telegram clusters.

2. EXPONENTIAL ACTIVITY DECAY:
• Formula: Weight(DC) = (sqrt(Bytes) / 100 + Conns * 25 + 1.0) * exp(-Δt / 60).
• Half-life T½ = 60 seconds. Every minute of inactivity cuts the DC activity weight in half.
• Upon reaching inactivity threshold (>180s), the socket is automatically closed or switched to standby sleep mode.
Status: Active • Cache: Video H.265 / Audio • Gateway: WSS

• Chat reading: 100% of WSS capacity is concentrated on DC2 (Amsterdam).\n• Media viewing: immediate transition to DC4 and FlowSeal CDN.\n• Background mode: inactive DC sockets enter sleep mode in 60 seconds.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:\n• For heavy downloads, proxy core adapts MTProto standby from 1 to 4 connections per active slot and sizes the buffer to measured BDP.\n• Bufferbloat control prevents equipment stalls under peak channel saturation.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:\n• Voice traffic is encoded using wideband Opus codec (48 kHz sample rate).\n• For seamless speech without robotic artifacts, jitter must stay under 15–25 ms with packet loss under 2%.

HOW IT WORKS:
• Standardized speech quality score (Mean Opinion Score) based on ITU-T G.107 E-Model ranging from 1.00 to 4.50.
• Factored from one-way delay d = RTT/2 + 2*Jitter, Opus wideband impairment factor (Ie), and packet loss percentage.

WHY IT MATTERS:
• Determines clarity and intelligibility of Telegram voice and video calls without echo, lag, or dropped speech.

BENCHMARKS:
• 4.20–4.50: HD Voice — studio grade with zero latency.
• 3.80–4.19: Good quality — natural comfortable conversation.
• 3.10–3.79: Acceptable — minor latency, intelligible voice.
• 2.40–3.09: Impaired — occasional stutter and syllable clipping.
• Below 2.40: Unusable for calls.

HOW IT WORKS:
• Min-RTT rolling window algorithm (60s, Google BBR style) measures pure physical line latency free of queue delay.
• Bufferbloat index (ΔRTT = SRTT - Min-RTT) calculates latent packet queuing inside carrier equipment during active data bursts.
• Dynamic filter (adaptive α from 0.125 to 0.50) calibrates smoothing rate to link stability.

WHY IT MATTERS:
• Reveals whether cell tower hardware buffers bloat during downloads, causing messaging lag and UI stalls.

BENCHMARKS:
• A+ (under 10 ms): pristine line with zero queuing.
• A (10–30 ms): negligible buffer buildup.
• B (30–75 ms): moderate bufferbloat.
• C (75–150 ms): elevated queuing delay.
• D (over 150 ms): severe bufferbloat.

SQI STABILITY INDEX (0–100%):
• Nonlinear sigmoidal utility function:
 - 45% weight on RTT (gradual decay beyond 60 ms).
 - 25% weight on LTE/Wi-Fi Jitter (penalty for jitter exceeding 10 ms).
 - 30% weight on probe delivery reliability with power loss factor.
• Explicit penalties applied for DPI drops, TLS handshakes, and Cloudflare 429 limits.

ITU-T G.107 VOICE SCORE (MOS 1.00–4.50):
• Transmission factor calculation R = 93.2 - Id(delay) - Ie(Opus impairments).
• Polynomial projection of R into speech perception MOS scale.

Happy Eyeballs ensures fast and reliable dual-stack (IPv6/IPv4) connection establishment.

• How it works: the client attempts an IPv6 connection first. If the handshake does not complete within the specified delay (default 200 ms), a parallel IPv4 connection is initiated. Whichever completes first handles the traffic, while the second is cleanly terminated.
• Choosing a delay: 100 ms favors faster fallback on low-latency networks; 200 ms is the RFC 8305 standard; 300 ms is suited for cellular connections with high jitter.

Controls how the DNS resolver and proxy engine handle internet protocol versions:

• Dual-Stack (IPv4/IPv6) — Default: queries both IPv4 and IPv6, choosing optimal routes via Happy Eyeballs.
• IPv4 Only — Disables IPv6 (AAAA queries). Recommended if your mobile carrier assigns broken local IPv6 routing that leads to connection hangs.
• IPv6 Preferred — Prioritizes IPv6 addresses when routing traffic to Telegram servers and Cloudflare gateways.

Sets the kernel receive (SO_RCVBUF) and send (SO_SNDBUF) buffer sizes for TCP sockets:

• 128 KB — Minimal footprint, saves RAM on entry-level devices and slow 2G/3G connections.
• 256 KB — Standard balanced default. Minimizes latency jitter (bufferbloat) while maintaining smooth chat sync.
• 512 KB – 1 MB — High throughput. Recommended for streaming high-bitrate video files on 4G/5G and Wi-Fi.
• 2 MB — Maximum buffer for high-bandwidth gigabit optical networks.

Specifies the frequency of heartbeat ping frames sent to Cloudflare Edge over WebSocket:

• Why use this: intermediate carrier gateways and home Wi-Fi routers drop idle NAT translations after 30–60 seconds of inactivity. Periodic pings keep the tunnel open.
• 15 sec — Maximum resilience on aggressive cellular carriers, prevents drops during idle intervals.
• 30 sec — Standard verified default, optimizes battery life while ensuring reliable notifications.
• 60 sec — Low-power mode for stable fixed broadband connections.
